query_log.findings: Autoware docs directly specify pose/twist inputs, covariance, time-delay handling, yaw-bias correction, Mahalanobis gating and pose/twist/odometry/covariance/diagnostics outputs. KITTI provides 22 odometry sequences, training ground truth, evaluation-only sequences and translation/rotation metrics; Boreas provides multimodal year-round weather data under CC BY 4.0. Open 2026 localization survey and course catalogues identify current/emerging learning-augmented and semantic approaches plus course outcomes. No inspectable future road-vehicle localization standard, future selectable tool/data product, credential or output contract was confirmed. Nigeria-related IO-VNBD evidence remains smartphone positioning, not Nigerian vehicle CAN/AV deployment. Opened the CMU Robotics Institute 1994 technical-report record. Its abstract describes a 3D asynchronous state-space navigation Kalman filter for autonomous-vehicle position estimation, including sensor integration, dead reckoning, INS/GPS, landmarks and map matching. The linked full PDF timed out, so the claim is limited to the abstract. Directly inspected the full open-access 2026 Springer survey, including ?2.2 lines 139-152: KF linear-Gaussian assumptions, EKF linearization, uncertainty outputs, limitations and sample-based/graph alternatives. ??1.1-1.2 and lines 118-125 define learning-augmented estimators (learned measurements/priors/pose regressors) and semantic/cognitive directions, with composition alongside classical back-ends. This supports an established KF/EKF techniques claim and a separate emerging learned-estimator claim; it does not support future deployment claims.
query_log.limits: Autoware pages document one stack and include PR-version pages; they do not establish universal contracts. KITTI is academic-use only and European data; Boreas has Canadian geography and CC BY 4.0. IO-VNBD country/sensor caveat remains. WEF roadmap is adoption forecast, not technical validation. Future and legal searches are bounded; they cannot prove universal absence. CMU report body was not available after a PDF fetch timeout; no equations, performance or full-text comparisons are claimed. The survey is secondary evidence; reported comparisons are heterogeneous, no unified performance ranking is warranted, and its research directions do not establish deployed vehicle products.
